# Coverage: what the lexical advice rule sees of the structural plans

<!-- Generated by `npm run coverage:matrix`. Statistics only: no source text. -->

`chat.unsolicited_advice` watches five phrases. The frozen action-plan features are structural.
These tables measure how much of the second the first also finds.

| Cell | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| both | The rule fires and the reply is plan-shaped |
| lexical only | The rule fires on something that is not a plan by structure |
| structural only | A plan the rule cannot see |
| neither | No plan, no marker |

## HelpSteer3, Chinese rows (4866 responses)

Permission is not known for this corpus — the user turns are ShareGPT conversations and their

| both | lexical only | structural only | neither |

Of the 210 plan-shaped responses, the rule finds 13 (6.2%).

## What this says, and what it does not

It says the two detectors are **not** a proxy and its target. They overlap on 13 firings out of 268,
and on HelpSteer3 the rule fires 45 times on replies that are not plan-shaped at all. The honest
description of `chat.unsolicited_advice` is therefore its firing condition — five phrases in a reply
whose user turn did not ask for advice — and not a claim about the behaviour behind it.

It does **not** say the rule should be removed, renamed or reweighted: a lexical rule is cheap,
deterministic and explainable, and none of that is in question. The lexical-only replies are the
ones that decide what it actually is, and reading them is the next piece of work.
